input_signals.name: Debt-Funded Tangible Capacity Expansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(GROWTH(ADD(ppent, invt), 1)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(SUB(dltis, dltr), DELTA(dlc, 1)), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Tangible capacity and inventory expansion financed by rising debt predicts lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Growth in PPE and inventory can be healthy if demand is strong, but debt-funded capacity expansion raises the risk of empire building, cyclically mistimed investment, or future financial constraints. Combining tangible investment growth with net debt issuance separates leveraged expansion from internally funded operating growth.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( growth( add( ppent, invt ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( add( sub( dltis, dltr ), delta( dlc, 1 ) ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: External-Funding Share of Capex
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(capx, at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), capx), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high industry-relative capex whose investment is largely covered by net external financing subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces total asset growth with actual capital spending, avoiding the near-identity between asset growth and net external financing. The net external-financing-to-capex ratio targets the funding source of investment rather than simply combining two broad published anomalies.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( capx, at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), capx ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dilutive Capex Shock
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), capx), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that sharply increase capex while relying on net equity issuance to fund that capex earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg uses net equity issuance rather than gross new claims, reducing contamination from debt rollover and routine financing churn. The investment leg is a capex shock relative to assets and industry peers, so the signal focuses on dilutive funding of incremental investment rather than static capex intensity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), capx ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net-Equity Soft-Asset Expansion
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ADD(intan, gdwl), at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that expand intangible assets and goodwill while issuing net equity subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Growth in soft assets often reflects acquisitions or hard-to-value investment where managers may overpay when their equity is expensive. Using net equity issuance rather than gross stock issuance repairs the financing-leg validation and better targets dilutive external funding.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( add( intan, gdwl ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Pre-Funded Capex Ramp
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1)), RANK(LAG(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that raise external capital before a subsequent capex ramp earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: Lagging the financing leg reduces the mechanical contemporaneous link between investment and net financing. The signal targets firms that first access external capital and then deploy it into accelerating investment, consistent with market timing or empire-building expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ), rank( lag( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Financed Hiring Spree
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(GROWTH(emp, 1), RATIO(capx, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms expanding both headcount and capex while issuing net long-term debt subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: Employment growth combined with capex identifies broader organizational expansion rather than a pure balance-sheet asset-growth effect. When that expansion is funded by net debt issuance, it may indicate late-cycle overconfidence, financial fragility, or empire building.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sumrank( growth( emp, 1 ), ratio( capx, at ) ), rank( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Net-Equity Capital Deepening
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(ppegt, emp), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that increase productive capital per employee while issuing net equity subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces split-contaminated share-count growth with accounting net equity proceeds, avoiding false dilution from stock splits or stock dividends. The investment leg is capital deepening rather than generic PPE or asset growth, targeting externally financed expansion of production capacity that may reflect market timing or overbuilding.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( delta( ratio( ppegt, emp ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Funded Inventory Overhang
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(invt, at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with industry-high inventory accumulation funded by net equity issuance earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The financing leg avoids the accounting-identity problem in total liabilities by using net equity proceeds rather than Δlt. Pairing inventory buildup with equity issuance focuses on a working-capital overhang or demand-misforecast channel, distinct from broad debt-funded tangible asset expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( invt, at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Debt-Funded Capex Cycle Peak
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, at), 5), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(dltis, dltr), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms issuing net long-term debt when capex intensity is near the top of their own recent investment cycle subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the smoothed capex-delta and equity-over-capex construction with a timing mechanism: external debt raised at a firm-specific capex peak. The signal is less about the average capex anomaly and more about late-cycle or overconfident investment financed with new leverage.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( capx, at ), 5 ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( dltis, dltr ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Short-Debt Inventory Funding Mismatch
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(invt, 1), ADD(capx, ABS(DELTA(invt, 1)))), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(dlc, 1), ADD(ABS(DELTA(dlc, 1)), ABS(SUB(dltis, dltr)))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose investment mix is dominated by inventory accumulation and funded relatively more with short-term debt subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids total-liability growth and instead focuses on a working-capital financing mismatch. Inventory-heavy investment funded by short-term borrowing can indicate demand overestimation, liquidity pressure, or fragile expansion rather than productive long-lived investment.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( delta( invt, 1 ), add( capx, abs( delta( invt, 1 ) ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( delta( dlc, 1 ), add( abs( delta( dlc, 1 ) ), abs( sub( dltis, dltr ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Funded Deal Hiring Bloat
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(RATIO(aqc, at), GROWTH(emp, 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), ADD(ABS(SUB(sstk, prstkc)), ABS(SUB(dltis, dltr)))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that combine acquisition spending and rapid hiring while relying disproportionately on net equity financing subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This moves away from the archived capex-shock × equity-issuance structure and focuses on organizational expansion around deals. The financing leg measures the equity share of active external financing, while the investment leg requires acquisition and employment expansion, targeting empire-building scale-ups rather than generic net share issuance.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sumrank( ratio( aqc, at ), growth( emp, 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), add( abs( sub( sstk, prstkc ) ), abs( sub( dltis, dltr ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Mix Labor-Asset Skew
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(GROWTH(emp, 1), GROWTH(ADD(ppent, invt), 1)), ADD(ABS(GROWTH(emp, 1)), ABS(GROWTH(ADD(ppent, invt), 1)))), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), ADD(ABS(SUB(sstk, prstkc)), ABS(SUB(dltis, dltr)))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose expansion is skewed toward labor rather than tangible operating assets and whose external financing mix is equity-heavy subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not a raw hiring-growth anomaly crossed with net issuance; both legs are relative mix measures. The investment leg captures labor-heavy scaling unsupported by commensurate PPE and inventory growth, while the financing leg asks whether active external funding is tilted toward equity rather than debt.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( winsor( ratio( sub( growth( emp, 1 ), growth( add( ppent, invt ), 1 ) ), add( abs( growth( emp, 1 ) ), abs( growth( add( ppent, invt ), 1 ) ) ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), add( abs( sub( sstk, prstkc ) ), abs( sub( dltis, dltr ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Cumulative External Investment Funding Share
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), at), 5)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(TS_SUM(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), 5), TS_SUM(ADD(capx, aqc), 5)), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with a rising multi-year investment trend and a high cumulative external-financing share of investment subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This builds on the strong portfolio evidence for persistent externally funded expansion but measures whether cumulative investment was actually financed externally. It should separate sustained self-funded investment programs from serial capital-market-funded expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( trend( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( ts_sum( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), 5 ), ts_sum( add( capx, aqc ), 5 ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stockpiled External Capex Ramp
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1)), RANK(LAG(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), DELTA(che, 1)), at), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Capex ramps following prior external financing that was retained as cash subsequently predict lower returns.
input_signals.reasoning: A simple lagged-financing signal may mix genuine prefunding with unrelated issuance, weakening portfolio evidence. Requiring prior external financing to coincide with cash accumulation targets firms that raised capital before deploying it into investment, consistent with market timing or planned empire building.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ) ), rank( lag( winsor( ratio( min( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), delta( che, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Deleveraging Investment Stretch
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), at)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(sstk, prstkc), dltr), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with high investment spending that issue net equity while retiring debt subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the problematic debt-rollover proxy with a distinct financing rotation: equity issuance used alongside debt repayment during an active investment program. Because cash is fungible, high capex plus equity-funded deleveraging suggests internal funds are insufficient or managers are exploiting overvalued equity while still expanding.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), at ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( min( sub( sstk, prstkc ), dltr ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Financed Inventory Capacity Skew
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(SUB(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, at), 5), TS_RANK(RATIO(ppent, at), 5))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), ADD(ABS(SUB(sstk, prstkc)), ABS(SUB(dltis, dltr)))), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with inventory unusually high relative to productive capacity and an equity-heavy external financing mix subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the debt-churn rollover leg and also avoids using contemporaneous inventory flow as a funding identity. The investment leg measures a firm-relative inventory-overhang state versus installed capacity, while the financing leg asks whether active external funding is tilted toward equity, consistent with overvaluation-funded working-capital expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( sub( ts_rank( ratio( invt, at ), 5 ), ts_rank( ratio( ppent, at ), 5 ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), add( abs( sub( sstk, prstkc ) ), abs( sub( dltis, dltr ) ) ) ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Stockpiled-Capital Inventory Overhang
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(invt, at), 5), RANK(LAG(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), DELTA(che, 1)), at), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that previously raised external capital and stockpiled it as cash, then later show inventory near a firm-specific peak, earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This tests whether pre-funded external capital is deployed into working-capital buildup rather than productive capacity. An inventory overhang following prior financing-and-cash accumulation can indicate demand overestimation or externally funded overexpansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( invt, at ), 5 ), rank( lag( winsor( ratio( min( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), delta( che, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Capex External Rescue
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), DELTA(che, 1)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that raise external capital after a prior capex ramp, especially when the financing is not accompanied by cash accumulation, subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This reverses the usual prefunding sequence and targets post-investment financing needs, which may reflect cost overruns, weak internal cash generation, or balance-sheet stress after expansion. Cash-adjusting the financing leg reduces the chance that the signal simply captures conservative liquidity raising.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), delta( che, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Deleveraging Preinvestment Ramp
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TREND(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), at), 3)), RANK(LAG(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(sstk, prstkc), dltr), at), 1), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that raise equity to retire debt before ramping investment subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This changes the mechanism from a contemporaneous equity-deleveraging investment stretch to a sequencing story: managers first rebuild debt capacity or exploit overvalued equity, then expand investment. Lagging the equity-funded debt retirement avoids a denominator rescaling and tests whether balance-sheet repair is followed by externally enabled expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( trend( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), at ), 3 ) ), rank( lag( winsor( ratio( min( sub( sstk, prstkc ), dltr ), at ), 1 ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Synchronous External Investment Peaks
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), at), 5)), RANK(TS_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms simultaneously near firm-specific peaks in investment intensity and net external financing subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the persistent-trend construction with a timing-of-extremes mechanism rather than another normalization of the same trend signal. The signal asks whether current investment and financing are unusually high for the same firm at the same time, consistent with opportunistic capital-market-funded expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_rank( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( ts_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Deal External Rescue
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(LAG(RATIO(aqc, at), 1), 5)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), DELTA(che, 1)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that raise external capital after a firm-specific acquisition spike, without retaining the proceeds as cash, subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This targets post-deal financing stress rather than the standard contemporaneous stock-financed-acquirer effect. A prior acquisition spike followed by cash-consumed external financing can indicate integration costs, overpayment, or weak internal cash generation after expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_rank( lag( ratio( aqc, at ), 1 ), 5 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), delta( che, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Capex Equity Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(sstk, prstkc), dltr), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that ramp capex and then issue equity while retiring debt subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This reverses the sequencing of equity-funded deleveraging before investment and tests whether a prior investment ramp forces balance-sheet repair. Equity issuance used alongside debt retirement after capex can indicate overvalued-equity market timing or external financing needed to restore debt capacity.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( min( sub( sstk, prstkc ), dltr ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory Spike Equity Rescue
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(ACCEL(RATIO(invt, at))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms with an accelerating inventory buildup that then rely on net equity issuance subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the persistent inventory-level rank with an inventory overhang event, reducing the chance that the signal merely identifies chronically inventory-heavy firms. The equity-financing leg targets a rescue-funding channel in which unexpected working-capital buildup is met with dilutive capital rather than internally generated cash.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( accel( ratio( invt, at ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Timed Investment Peak
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), at), 5)), RANK(TS_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(sstk, prstkc), at), 1), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms simultaneously near firm-specific peaks in investment intensity and net equity issuance subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This avoids the cash-consumed sources-uses overlap by focusing specifically on equity market timing rather than total external funds net of cash. The mechanism is that unusually high investment coinciding with an unusually high equity-issuance state may reveal overvaluation-funded expansion, not merely accounting deployment of funds.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ts_rank( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), at ), 5 ) ), rank( ts_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sstk, prstkc ), at ), 1 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Post-Capex Equity Cash-Use Rescue
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(DELTA(RATIO(capx, at), 1), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(SUB(sstk, prstkc), DELTA(che, 1))), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that issue equity after a capex ramp, without simply retaining the proceeds as cash, subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This decomposes the strong post-capex external-rescue mechanism into the dilutive equity channel while requiring the equity proceeds to be economically consumed rather than stockpiled. The lagged capex shock reduces contemporaneous sources-uses mechanical overlap and captures financing stress or market-timed issuance after expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( delta( ratio( capx, at ), 1 ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( min( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( sub( sstk, prstkc ), delta( che, 1 ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Constrained Post-Investment Issuer
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(RANK(LAG(TS_RANK(RATIO(ADD(capx, aqc), at), 5), 1)), RANK(LAG(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(che, at), 1)), 1))), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that recently combined high investment intensity with cash depletion and then issue external capital subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This repairs the earlier cash-burned investment sequencing idea by requiring both prior high investment and prior cash drawdown, rather than allowing pure cash decliners to dominate. Current external issuance after that constrained state is consistent with emergency financing, cost overruns, or weak internal cash generation following expansion.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( rank( lag( ts_rank( ratio( add( capx, aqc ), at ), 5 ), 1 ) ), rank( lag( neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ), 1 ) ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( sub( add( sstk, dltis ), add( prstkc, dltr ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Inventory-Shock Equity Deleveraging
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(ACCEL(RATIO(invt, at)), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(sstk, prstkc), dltr), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms that experience an inventory buildup shock and then issue equity while retiring debt subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: The investment leg captures an inventory overhang event rather than a persistent inventory-heavy level. Subsequent equity-funded deleveraging after that shock can signal working-capital stress, demand disappointment, or external capital raised to repair the balance sheet after an operating misstep.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( lag( accel( ratio( invt, at ) ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( min( sub( sstk, prstkc ), dltr ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capex-Peak Equity Cash Use
input_signals.expression: MUL(TS_RANK(RATIO(capx, at), 5), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(SUB(sstk, prstkc), DELTA(che, 1))), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms investing near their own capex-cycle peak while issuing equity that is not retained as cash subsequently underperform.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes the equity-deleveraging leg and instead tests whether equity issuance is being consumed during a firm-specific investment peak. The mechanism is overvaluation-funded or liquidity-constrained expansion, distinct from merely issuing equity to retire debt or from a TS_RANK equity-timing recombination.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ts_rank( ratio( capx, at ), 5 ), rank( winsor( ratio( min( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( sub( sstk, prstkc ), delta( che, 1 ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Equity-Funded Replacement Burden
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, DELTA(ppegt, 1)), at), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(MIN(SUB(sstk, prstkc), SUB(SUB(sstk, prstkc), DELTA(che, 1))), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose capex does not translate into gross productive-capacity growth, while issuing equity that is consumed rather than stockpiled, earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the noisy TS_RANK of PPE changes with an economically interpretable capex-minus-gross-PPE-build gap, capturing replacement burden, cost overruns, or unproductive investment. Pairing that burden with consumed equity issuance identifies firms funding non-self-sustaining investment needs through dilutive external capital.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( capx, delta( ppegt, 1 ) ), at ), 1 ) ), rank( winsor( ratio( min( sub( sstk, prstkc ), sub( sub( sstk, prstkc ), delta( che, 1 ) ) ), at ), 1 ) ) )

input_signals.name: Replacement-Burden External Rescue
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(LAG(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(capx, DELTA(ppegt, 1)), at), 1), 1)), RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ADD(sstk, dltis), ADD(prstkc, dltr)), DELTA(che, 1)), at), 1)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms whose prior capex did not translate into gross PPE growth and that then raise external capital not retained as cash earn lower future returns.
input_signals.reasoning: The lagged investment leg targets unproductive or replacement-heavy capex while reducing contemporaneous sources-and-uses overlap. Current cash-consumed external financing then acts as a rescue-funding signal after a weak investment conversion episode.
input_signals.author: proposer
